A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SurgBlood and BlooDet, and all supplied pages are readable. However, neither file contains appendices, while v3 references unavailable supplementary sections B, C, E, F, G and H. The main papers support comparison, but the referenced additional experiments, training algorithm and annotation-agreement analysis cannot be inspected.

before.justification: V2 reports original SurgBlood benchmark results in Table 1 and component, edge-generator and optical-flow ablations in Tables 2-4.

after.justification: V3 reports original SurgBlood and zero-shot HemoSet results, adapted-baseline comparisons and ablations in Tables 2-7.

M1.justification: The architecture, optical-flow compensation, prompt mechanisms and four loss components are retained. V3 newly specifies alternating frozen-branch updates in Section 4.4, whereas v2 states a combined loss without specifying update order. The PDFs do not establish whether this changes the procedure or documents an existing implementation; v3's referenced training algorithm is unavailable.

E1.justification: V2 evaluates only human cholecystectomy videos from SurgBlood. V3 adds region detection on HemoSet animal robotic-surgery videos, substantially extending the evaluated population and environment. Rabbani and SUN-SEG evaluations are also mentioned, but their results are confined to the unavailable supplement.

E2.justification: V3 adds evaluated STDDNet, CalibratedSL and ConsisTNet baselines, while SAM-Adapter and SAM2-Adapter disappear from the supplied comparisons. It also evaluates dual-task adaptations of region-only and point-only methods alongside their task-specific versions; v2's corresponding adaptation was limited to SAM 2 with an added point head.

E3.justification: V3 introduces zero-shot HemoSet testing using SurgBlood-trained models and systematic comparisons between single-task models and versions with additional prediction heads. The SurgBlood 75/20 clip split, metrics and 20-epoch training budget remain unchanged. The reported source-case count changes from 41 to 42, without establishing that data were recollected.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, v3 adds cross-dataset transfer testing and systematic single-task versus dual-task analysis. Figure 6 adds an optical-flow motion-compensation case study, and Figure 9 adds joint removal of mask maps and mask memory. Additional analyses referenced only in the missing supplement cannot be assessed.

E5.justification: V2 reports point estimates, whereas v3 reports mean and standard deviation throughout the main comparisons in Tables 2-4. This is a substantial expansion of uncertainty reporting, although run counts, seeds and the source of variability are unspecified. The ablation tables still report point estimates.

E6.justification: BlooDet's SurgBlood point estimates remain unchanged, including 64.88 IoU, 78.70 Dice and 83.69 PCK-10%. V3 adds HemoSet results of 59.62 IoU and 74.70 Dice and numerous baseline entries. Ablation IoU changes from 50.93 to 56.22 without EG/PMM and from 60.79 to 62.41 without the Laplacian filter. Newly adapted dual-task baselines are different conditions, not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: V3 adds a coupled optimization definition in Equation 1, conditional branch-update equations in Equations 10-11, and a joint-fixed-point rationale. These extend the mathematical treatment beyond v2's combined loss, but no convergence proof is supplied. The optical-flow and edge-filter equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the SurgBlood benchmark and SAM 2-based joint bleeding-region and point detection using edge prompts, point memory and bidirectional guidance. The updated comparator count and expanded evaluations support the same core superiority claim rather than redefining the principal contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds an explanation of mutual geometric and spatial constraints between the tasks and interprets alternating updates as mutual adaptation. Section 5.3 also interprets the paired baseline comparisons as evidence of task interference and the benefits of its optimization strategy. The earlier explanations of edge enhancement and background-flow stability are retained.

D1.justification: V3 adds explicit branch-update instructions and changes the abstract's code/data statement from future availability to current availability, without providing an access URL. Conversely, v2's explicit exclusion of absent points from the point-loss calculation is no longer stated. Hardware, input resolution, learning rates, optimizer and training duration remain documented as before.

R1.justification: V3 adds positioning against Rabbani's bleeding dataset, ReSurgSAM2 and the newly evaluated baseline papers, including a dataset-comparison table. It removes the separate large-vision-model video-segmentation discussion and several associated citations. The overarching positioning around temporal modeling and cross-task guidance remains intact.

P1.justification: The six-section narrative and much of the wording are retained. V3 condenses the introduction and related work, removes introductory paragraph labels, numbers the dataset subsections and reframes the loss discussion as an objective-function section. These are localized structural and language revisions.

P2.justification: V3 changes the paper from single-column to two-column layout, redraws the framework diagrams and reorganizes dataset statistics. It expands the benchmark display into Tables 2-4, adds a dataset-comparison table and optical-flow figure, and replaces the mutual-guidance bar chart with radar plots containing an additional variant.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses v2's exclusively SurgBlood-based evaluation with visible zero-shot HemoSet evidence and makes comparisons more informative through paired single-task and dual-task baselines. These support a limited quality gain. The benefit is tempered by removal of the strong SAM2-Adapter comparator, unspecified uncertainty-estimation details and unavailable supplementary material; the new training description also leaves the actual procedural change unresolved.
